To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the benefits of social capital in interfirm and intrafirm networks are different.
the degree of knowledge transfer from alliance partners depends on the structure of relationships within the multidivisional organization.

1) the private benefits of brokerage and centralization are more important in interfirm networks than in intrafirm networks, whereas 2) the collective benefits of closure and low levels are more important in intrafirm networks than in interfirm networks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the process through which social capital is translated into knowledge acquisition.
the process through which the social capital of a firm's network structure translates into knowledge acquisition from the firm's alliance partners.
how the social capital of the firm's network of partners translates into knowledge acquisition from those partners.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more a network is characterized by closure, the less brokerage is required to achieve the same level of social capital.
, as the number of alliance partners increases, the knowledge acquisition benefits from the network increase up to a certain point, after which the benefits decrease.
the results of this study indicate that the network of alliances is a key determinant of the firm's ability to acquire new knowledge from alliance partners.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more central the unit, the more it will benefit from its own network, whereas the more peripheral the unit, the better it will do by relying on the network of other units.
we have developed a theory of the role of social capital in the process of knowledge acquisition from external sources, in the context of the multinational firm.
the social capital perspective is a powerful tool to understand the dynamics of interfirm networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the distribution of social capitals benefits within the organization is an important determinant of the degree of knowledge acquisition.
the benefits of social capital are distributed unevenly within organizations.
knowledge transfer from alliance partners is a function of both the external network structure and the internal network structure of the focal company.
